<a id="bless_the_rains"></a>
## Soft-Rock: `bless_the_rains.yml`

An early eighties soft-rock song in the manner of Africa (Toto), with a melody of its own. The verse
is low and quiet and the chorus an anthem: the tune leaps up an octave and holds long high notes in
three-part harmony over big drums, a driving bass, brass and strings. The verse is in D major on I
iii vi and the chorus a whole step down, in C major, on vi IV I V, as the song changes key; a brass
riff on IV iii vi opens and returns; a marimba figure, congas and a flute solo.

<a id="chord_progression_generator"></a>
## Progressions: `06_chord_progression_generator.yml`

A pop song in C major made from three patterns one bar long, an arpeggio, a bass figure and a
chord pad, each written over chord I and played through a Progression, a different one in every
scene: Pop, Fifties, Andalusian in A minor, Pachelbel's eight chords, Pop again with the pad's
chords inverted so that they move less, and Pop with the pad through a Voice leading generator.

<a id="follow_chords"></a>
## Follow Chords: `24_follow_chords.yml`

A song in A minor whose chords are written in one place, a muted track called SILENT Chords. The bass,
the pad and the arpeggio each play one bar, written over chord I, through a Follow Chords
generator that moves their notes to whatever chord that track plays. The chords are heard plainly
first, then the band plays without following and sounds stuck on one chord, then the bass follows
alone, then everyone. Later scenes add a tune, change the chords under the same patterns, change
chord twice a bar, and follow chords that a Progression makes on that track.

<a id="goodnight_world"></a>
## Synth-Pop: `goodnight_world.yml`

An early eighties synth-pop song in the manner of Sweet Dreams (Eurythmics), with a melody of its
own. A two-bar synth riff in eighths, two synths an octave apart, over i for a bar and VI and v for
half a bar each; a pre-chorus on VI V i iv and a bridge on a suspended i and a major IV.

<a id="peanut_buttercup"></a>
## Soul-Pop: `peanut_buttercup.yml`

A late sixties soul-pop song in the manner of Build Me Up Buttercup (The Foundations), with a melody
of its own. It starts on its chorus, as the song does: I, a dominant chord on III, IV and V, two
bars each, the voices answering each clause, then I, its seventh, IV turning minor and home; the
verse goes I V bVII IV; three hits and an answer on IV, iii and ii, and held notes rising on V.

<a id="phrasing"></a>
## Phrasing: `25_phrasing.yml`

A slow ballad in A minor whose tune is heard as written and then through a Phrasing generator with
one setting changed in each scene: a deep breath after each line, a rise and fall of loudness, choppy
notes, and flowing notes on the tune written short. The last two scenes are a verse and a chorus sung
with the settings together.

<a id="rick_rolling"></a>
## Dance-Pop: `rick_rolling.yml`

A late eighties dance-pop song in the manner of Never Gonna Give You Up (Rick Astley), with a melody
of its own. Two chords a bar: IV V iii vi under the string hook and the chorus, IV V in the verse; a
drum fill opens, the band stops before each chorus, and the voice sits low.
